title: Responsive column collapse and keyboard navigation for virtual tables
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and spec a responsive behavior for wide virtualized tables where columns can automatically collapse into a prioritized overflow, while preserving full keyboard accessibility and table features (sorting, filtering, column resizing, selection). Deliver updated component patterns, interaction spec, and tokens adjustments for density modes.
problem_statement: Large datasets frequently have many columns that do not fit on narrow screens or at compact density. Current virtualized table UX clips columns and relies on horizontal scroll which hurts discoverability and keyboard users. We need a consistent collapse/overflow pattern that works with virtualization, preserves user control over column order/visibility, and supports keyboard-first resizing, sorting, and filtering.
proposed_solution: Introduce a responsive column collapse mode that: 1) automatically groups low-priority columns into an overflow panel when available width is insufficient, 2) exposes a persistent 'More columns' affordance that opens a keyboard-focusable flyout with full table controls, 3) provides keyboard-accessible column resize handles and column visibility toggles, and 4) integrates with virtualization by rendering collapsed columns only inside the flyout. Provide updated density tokens to ensure consistent spacing and hit targets across compact/regular/comfortable modes.
design_decisions: Automatic collapse uses column priority metadata (column.priority: high|medium|low) rather than only width heuristics to avoid collapsing actionable columns.
Overflow flyout will be a focus-trapped, ARIA-compliant dialog that mirrors table controls (sort, filter, resize, hide/show) to keep parity for keyboard-only users.

Column resize interactions will support both drag and arrow-key adjustments. Arrow-key increments follow tokenized step sizes (token: spacing-step-xs) and expose live-preview while respecting virtualization cache boundaries.

Virtualization will not render collapsed columns in the main viewport to avoid wasted render cost; collapsed columns render on demand inside the flyout with a separate small virtualization window to handle very large column counts.
We will prioritize manual override: users can pin columns to prevent collapse and reorder columns; pin state persists in local storage and via API opt-in (future work for cloud persistence).
Animations kept subtle (scale+fade) and optional via a motion token to support reduced-motion accessibility preferences.
We will not auto-collapse columns that contain selection checkboxes, primary entity cell, or inline actions to avoid breaking core interactions.
Density token updates limited to spacing and hit-target changes to avoid visual regressions elsewhere; provide a migration guide for components using table spacing tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Given a wide dataset and compact density, the table collapses low-priority columns into the overflow flyout when viewport width < collapse threshold and the More columns button is visible.
Keyboard users can open the flyout via keyboard, tab to hidden column controls, and perform sort/filter/resizing operations without a mouse.
Column resize via keyboard updates column width visually and emits width-change events documented in component API.
Virtualization performance: main table render cost does not increase when columns are collapsed; measured frame times remain within existing SLOs for typical datasets (baseline measurement attached).
Design tokens and density presets included in the PRD and implemented in the Figma library; front-end has samples for compact/regular/comfortable densities.
Edge case: tables with fixed-width pinned columns do not have those pinned columns collapsed and maintain sticky positioning.
Developer handoff includes component props: collapseThreshold, columnPriority, persistPinState, keyboardResizeStep, and ariaSpec link.
Accessibility audit completed (WCAG keyboard navigation and screen reader flows), with at most two minor issues to resolve before final review.
user_research: Moderated usability test with 6 participants (PM/BI users) showed 4/6 preferred overflow flyout to horizontal scroll on small viewports.
Accessibility review session with 2 a11y specialists on 2025-02-20 produced recommended keyboard focus flow changes (see comments).
